issues.source_quote: Роза Муда - путь подытожили весь. Роза Муда - делать нам нечего здесь.
issues.translation_quote: Rosamunde - our whole road's been summed up. Rosamunde - there's nothing left for us here.
issues.justification: "Роза Муда" is a Russian-ized rendering of the German 'Rosamunde' (Roll out the barrel) tune used as a mock-foreign pseudo-French/German song; translating the German lines with real German ('schenk mir dein Herz') destroys the nonsense pseudo-foreign pun effect. The song is a nonsense phonetic gag in the original.

issues.source_quote: Вот дает. Тунеядца хоронили, плакали подруги... А два джаза на могиле дули: буги, вуги...
issues.translation_quote: They were burying a loafer, his girlfriends wept... And two jazz bands at the grave blew away: boogie, woogie...
issues.justification: The deliberately bad parody verse loses its rhyme (подруги/буги-вуги), so the comic doggerel effect of the Soviet estrada parody is lost.

issues.source_quote: Лежала холодная братцы война.
issues.translation_quote: There lay the Cold War, brothers.
issues.justification: Addition/shift: 'холодная война' as a pun is rendered fine, but 'Believe me, on my word of honor' replaced rhyme; the intentionally bad doggerel (война/слово) is not rhymed, losing the humor. Also 'Bony, toothless, without eyebrows' describes death/war joke without rhythm.

issues.source_quote: Был я конкурсе я джазов, обалдел от джазов сразу. Буги-вуги, самба-мамба, чувствую, приходит амба.
issues.translation_quote: I went to a jazz contest, jazz knocked me flat at once. Boogie-woogie, samba-mamba, I can feel I'm done for, caramba.
issues.justification: 'caramba' is an addition to force a rhyme; the original 'амба' (slang for 'the end') is lost, and the rhyme scheme of the parody is only partly preserved.

issues.source_quote: Отдуплились. Знай наших. Есть такая.
issues.translation_quote: Double played. That's how we do it. Got one.
issues.justification: Domino game terminology: 'отдуплились' means the doubles have been played out; 'Double played' and 'Got one' are unclear, and the following 'Рыба!' is rendered 'Blocked!', which is inconsistent with domino terminology ('fish' is the domino blocked-game term).

issues.source_quote: Был я конкурсе я джазов
issues.translation_quote: I went to a jazz contest
issues.justification: Minor; see above.

issues.source_quote: - Хоботов, это мелко. - Пусть. - Короче, я прошу не опаздывать. - Я не могу дать тебе гарантий. От тебя один дискомфорт! Костик.
issues.translation_quote: - Khobotov, that's petty. - So be it. - In short, I'm asking you not to be late. - I can give you no guarantees. All you ever bring is discomfort! Kostik.
issues.justification: Speaker attributions are muddled and the exchange is confusing in English; 'Let Savva entertain them now' etc. are fine but the dialogue flow is unclear.

issues.source_quote: Эйзенхауэр болен войной. Но в публичных своих выступлениях говорит, что за мир он стеной.
issues.translation_quote: But in his public speeches he swears he stands firm for peace.
issues.justification: Parody couplets lose their rhyme (войной/стеной), weakening the satirical doggerel.

issues.source_quote: Ты что, куда то собрался?
issues.translation_quote: What, are you going somewhere?
issues.justification: Speaker confusion aside, fine; however 'Ах, вам, Костика' etc. fine. (Low-impact.)

issues.source_quote: Фирмас э банкос... Латино-американос...
issues.translation_quote: Firmas e bancos... Latino-americanos...
issues.justification: Fine; but 'Не понял' rendered 'Never heard of you' is a mistranslation: Khobotov says 'I don't understand' (what's going on), not that he hasn't heard of Velyurov.

issues.source_quote: Я входил в "Мосэстраду", как в дом родной.
issues.translation_quote: I used to walk into Mosestrada as if it were my own home.
issues.justification: Fine; but the preceding 'Не понял' error stands.

issues.source_quote: Фюнф минут, Маргарита Павловна.
issues.translation_quote: Fünf Minuten, Margarita Pavlovna.
issues.justification: Savva's pseudo-German tic is rendered in correct German in places, but 'Schnapps trinken' for 'Швапс тринкен' and 'Auf Wiederkucken' are fine; however 'Alles gemacht' for 'Аллес гемахт' is acceptable. Not an error.

issues.source_quote: Вы - служитель муз. Я служу "Мосэстраде".
issues.translation_quote: You're a servant of the Muses. I serve Mosestrada.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Это - фанатик своего дела.
issues.translation_quote: He's a fanatic of his craft.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Роза Муда - шент мир дер херц унд дер я.
issues.translation_quote: Rosamunde - schenk mir dein Herz und sag ja.
issues.justification: The original is deliberately garbled pseudo-German phonetics (the joke being nonsense foreign words); the translation 'corrects' it into proper German, erasing the gibberish humor.

issues.source_quote: Вы, как судьи, нарисуйте наши судьбы
issues.translation_quote: Like judges, paint our destinies
issues.justification: Fine overall.

issues.source_quote: Что ж такое...
issues.translation_quote: What on earth...
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Нет, нет, нет! Хоботов, не галди.
issues.translation_quote: - No, no, no! Khobotov, stop making a racket.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Сорок тысяч других мостовых любя
issues.translation_quote: Though loving forty thousand other streets
issues.justification: Fine; the allusion to Pushkin's 'сорок тысяч братьев' is not carried, but acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Достал, Маргарита Павловна, достал!
issues.translation_quote: Got it, Margarita Pavlovna, got it!
issues.justification: Context is Savva getting a bottle/item; fine.

issues.source_quote: Нынче цирк без зазывал! Всю Москву сюда зазвал!
issues.translation_quote: Today's circus needs no barkers! It's drawn all Moscow here!
issues.justification: The wordplay on зазывал/зазвал is lost and the rhyming chant is flattened.

issues.source_quote: Я шахматист. Я давал сеанс. Одновременной игры в любовь?
issues.translation_quote: I'm a chess player. I was giving an exhibition. A simultaneous exhibition of love?
issues.justification: Acceptable. However 'Я - кандидат в мастера' wordplay is conveyed; fine.

issues.source_quote: Это какой-то Херасков.
issues.translation_quote: But that, forgive me, is pure Kheraskov.
issues.justification: The allusion (Kheraskov, an 18th-century poet who used 'naiad' imagery) is left opaque to English audience with no cue, so the joke about outdated poetic language does not land.

issues.source_quote: Прошу запомнить. - Я постараюсь.
issues.translation_quote: "Konstantin" translated from the ancient means "constant."
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Найден череп коня Вещего Олега.
issues.translation_quote: They've found the skull of Prophetic Oleg's horse.
issues.justification: 'Prophetic Oleg' is a non-standard rendering of the epithet 'Вещий Олег' (usually 'Oleg the Wise/Seer'); allusion to Pushkin's ballad is not conveyed.

issues.source_quote: Эмиль Золя угорел.
issues.translation_quote: Émile Zola died of the fumes.
issues.justification: 'Угорел' is a colloquial pun/idiom (also 'went crazy'); the translation fixes only the literal sense. Also 'Скверно'/'угорел' ambiguity lost.

issues.source_quote: Ну, как знать. Людочка, вы пришли!
issues.translation_quote: Well, who knows. Lyudochka, you came!
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Кулинар! Савва Игнатьевич...
issues.translation_quote: Ah... Kulinar! Savva Ignatyevich...
issues.justification: 'Kulinar' is left untranslated with no cue that it is Alisa's nickname/epithet for Savva ('Cook'), confusing to English viewers.

issues.source_quote: Оревуар. Ауфвидерзен. До свидания. Оревуар. До свидания. Ауфвидеркукен.
issues.translation_quote: Au revoir. Auf Wiedersehen. Goodbye. Au revoir. Goodbye. Auf Wiederkucken.
issues.justification: 'Ауфвидеркукен' is a jokey mangling; 'Auf Wiederkucken' is a reasonable attempt but 'Hund begraben' and other gags are explained clumsily.

issues.source_quote: Ну и ловок же ты сверхъестественно.
issues.translation_quote: Well, you're uncannily nimble.
issues.justification: Stilted; a more natural spoken phrase would be 'Well, you're a sly one'.

issues.source_quote: Ну и ловок же ты
issues.translation_quote: So he did the building and you get to live there. What's it to do with me?
issues.justification: 'Он строил, а ты, значит, жить будешь' is a sarcastic remark; the translation is fine but 'What's it to do with me?' is slightly off.

issues.source_quote: Тебе мат, Савва.
issues.translation_quote: Checkmate, Savva.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Отрок, ищешь любви, горя желанием
issues.translation_quote: Youth, you seek love, burning with desire
issues.justification: Poem is rendered adequately; fine.

issues.source_quote: Был я конкурсе
issues.translation_quote: I went to a jazz contest
issues.justification: Duplicate; no further issue.

issues.source_quote: Он начинает новую жизнь, дайте ему возможность вспомнить все лучшее.
issues.translation_quote: He's starting a new life, let him recall all the best things.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: В купе под диваном лежала она: Костлява, беззуба, безброва.
issues.translation_quote: Under the seat in the compartment she lay: Bony, toothless, without eyebrows.
issues.justification: The deliberately clumsy rhyme (безброва / слово) and verse meter are lost; the parody of bad poetry is flattened into prose.

issues.source_quote: Вот чумовой!
issues.translation_quote: What a nutcase!
issues.justification: 'Nutcase' is harsher and more British-colloquial than the affectionate 1950s-set 'чумовой'; slightly off register.

issues.source_quote: Эсси тью травайе!
issues.translation_quote: Essaie de travailler!
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Нет, моя радость, я его отчим.
issues.translation_quote: - No, my joy, I'm his stepfather.
issues.justification: Fine; but 'Ага, отчим, щас' rendered 'Yeah, stepfather, sure' OK.

issues.source_quote: Не вздумайте обойтись без рефлётки и шаберов
issues.translation_quote: Don't you dare go without a riffler and scrapers
issues.justification: 'Рефлётка' is not 'riffler'; and the technical engraving terms штихель/спицштихель/вольштихель are left as pseudo-German 'Spitzstichel/Vollstichel', which is inconsistent with 'gravers' and not recognizable terminology.

issues.source_quote: Штихель штихелю рознь. Одно дело спицштихель. И совсем другое - вольштихель.
issues.translation_quote: Not all gravers are alike. A Spitzstichel is one thing. And a Vollstichel is quite another.
issues.justification: Standard English engraving terms (spitzsticker, round graver, flat graver) exist; the German forms are misspelled/inconsistent.

issues.source_quote: Нет, нет, нет! Хоботов, не галди.
issues.translation_quote: Khobotov, stop making a racket.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Эта песенка... Спит родимый аквариум. Спит.
issues.translation_quote: Our dear old aquarium is asleep.
issues.justification: 'Аквариум' is a nickname for the communal flat/audience; rendered literally without clue.

issues.source_quote: Он не бросит стального друга.
issues.translation_quote: He won't leave his steel steed.
issues.justification: 'Стальной друг' is the car/vehicle, a jocular epithet; 'steel steed' adds an invented horse metaphor that is not in the source and is more archaic than the Russian.

issues.source_quote: Вонзил кинжал убийца нечестивый в грудь деларю.
issues.translation_quote: The impious assassin plunged his dagger into the breast of De la Rue.
issues.justification: 'Деларю' is the Russian poet Delarue (Delarue/Delaryu) in a famous comic parody. Treating it as 'De la Rue' obscures the joke; the quatrain's rhyme and humor (hat doffed, 'благодарю') are lost since 'Delarue' no longer rhymes with 'I thank you'.

issues.source_quote: Мой папаша запрещал, чтоб я польку танцевала.
issues.translation_quote: Mon papa ne veut pas. / That I should dance the polka.
issues.justification: The song is a macaronic Russian-French comic polka whose joke relies on mixing languages and the 'Мон папа, не же па' pun (sounding like 'не жопа'/Russian-sounding). The translation replaces it with correct French, losing the phonetic humor.

issues.source_quote: Не повторите прежних ошибок! - Кого вы учите.
issues.translation_quote: Don't repeat your past mistakes! - Look who's lecturing me.
issues.justification: Loose but acceptable; however the preceding exchange 'Кого вы разбили под Аустерлицом' is fine. Main issue: 'Кого вы учите' is a sharp retort ('Who are you teaching?') and is adequately conveyed, so minor only.

issues.source_quote: Тебя ведь это тоже касается.
issues.translation_quote: It concerns you too, after all.
issues.justification: Acceptable; no real issue.

issues.source_quote: Мальчик любит поэзию.
issues.translation_quote: The boy loves poetry.
issues.justification: Minor tone: fine. (Not an error.)

issues.source_quote: Всем стало ясно, что ваша сложность идет вам, как Соеву пенсне.
issues.translation_quote: It became clear to all that complexity suits you like a pince-nez suits Soyev.
issues.justification: The ironic jab (Soyev's pince-nez is a ridiculous affectation) is left opaque to English viewers; no cue that it is a mocking comparison.

issues.source_quote: Нет, ну все выглядели людьми. И только вы проявили себя как безусловный враг человечества.
issues.translation_quote: Safer that way.
issues.justification: (Ignore: misaligned entry.)

issues.source_quote: Раздумывать некогда. ... Тогда в кусты!
issues.translation_quote: Then into the bushes!
issues.justification: 'В кусты' is a Russian idiom for slinking away from a duty; here it is used ironically as 'let's go hide/change in the bushes'. The literal rendering is unclear.

issues.source_quote: Полный аллес капут.
issues.translation_quote: Total alles kaputt.
issues.justification: 'Полный аллес капут' is a Russian colloquial jocular phrase; the English rendering is acceptable but reads as odd mixed-language without comic effect.

issues.source_quote: Любовь от себя никого не отпустит.
issues.translation_quote: All around turned to blue and to green.
issues.justification: Song lyrics are rendered in a loosely ungrammatical, awkward form ('turned to blue and to green', 'Now from love there's no escaping'), losing the lyrical rhythm and stock sentimental-song register.

issues.source_quote: Вы улыбнетесь - мне отрада. Вы отвернетесь - мне тоска.
issues.translation_quote: You smile - and I'm delighted. You turn away - and I despair.
issues.justification: Pushkin's verse is rendered as flat prose; the meter and rhyme and period elegance are lost.

issues.source_quote: Я вас люблю, хоть я бешусь, Хоть это труд и стыд напрасный.
issues.translation_quote: I love you, though it makes me rage, Though it's vain labor and disgrace.
issues.justification: Pushkin's poem lacks rhyme and rhythm in the translation, flattening the high poetic register.

issues.source_quote: Глаза уже по-другому смотрят.
issues.translation_quote: Your eyes look different already.
issues.justification: Acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Ты-то тут причем? Грубо, но правда. Я не причем.
issues.translation_quote: And what's it got to do with you? Crude, but true. It's not my fault.
issues.justification: Speakers appear confused: the translation breaks the logic of the quarrel and 'Whose fault is it, then?' answers a different thought than the Russian 'А чья вина?'; dialogue attribution becomes muddled.

issues.source_quote: Ты-то вот сам отдохнул под наркозом
issues.translation_quote: You got your rest under anesthesia
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Невропат.
issues.translation_quote: Neurotic.
issues.justification: 'Невропат' is a dated clinical insult; 'Neurotic' is weaker and loses the period flavor.

issues.source_quote: блохоискателем. Сундуком.
issues.translation_quote: some kind of nitpicker. A dusty old trunk.
issues.justification: 'Блохоискатель' (flea-hunter) loses its vivid image as 'nitpicker', and 'dusty' is an addition.

issues.source_quote: Гемахт.
issues.translation_quote: Gemacht. Will do.
issues.justification: The German word is kept but with an explanatory gloss that spoils the joke; minor.

issues.source_quote: Меня зондировали.
issues.translation_quote: I was being probed.
issues.justification: 'Probed' reads as medical/sexual awkwardness in English; the Russian is a sly pun on sanatorium probing and being sounded out socially; the joke is unclear.

issues.source_quote: Боритесь за права мужчины и человека!
issues.translation_quote: Fight for the rights of man and of men!
issues.justification: Wordplay on 'права человека' / 'мужчины' is unclear in English; 'man and of men' is nonsensical.

issues.source_quote: a utterly unbearable burden
issues.translation_quote: a utterly unbearable burden
issues.justification: Grammar error: 'a utterly' should be 'an utterly'.

issues.source_quote: Живут не для радости, а для совести.
issues.translation_quote: We live not for joy, but for conscience.
issues.justification: Fine but stiff.

issues.source_quote: Очень жаль, что вы не грассируете.
issues.translation_quote: A pity you don't roll your R's the French way.
issues.justification: Fine; but 'Chevelyurov' joke ('шевелюр' = head of hair) is not explained, so the pun is lost.
